mainTopic: Two cross-comparison questions between שבת and יום טוב: (1) May one clear produce off a roof on יום טוב until the floor is fully exposed, given the Shabbos rule against emptying an entire אוצר? (2) May one move sacks from house to house on שבת, given the יום טוב rule against carrying produce מגג לגג?
overview: The גמרא first asks a series of mirror-image questions between שבת and יום טוב. May one clear a roof completely on יום טוב, given the שבת rule against emptying a whole אוצר? May sacks be moved from roof to roof, or lowered by rope and ladder, on שבת, given the limits on saving produce on יום טוב? Each question has reasons pulling both ways: the severity of the day, the מצוה of learning, people's casual attitude toward יום טוב, and the loss of produce. The series ends with תיקו. Next, on the משנה's rule that one may cover produce, עולא says even bricks may be covered, while רבי יצחק allows only usable items, because a כלי may be handled only for something that is not מוקצה. Proofs from the משנה's wording are pushed off. Then four challenges against רבי יצחק (a leak, bricks, stones, a beehive) are each answered by showing the item is usable. The beehive answer is pressed further, through winter honeycombs, planning ahead, and whether the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה or רבי שמעון. It ends with the whole ברייתא following רבי יהודה, about a hive with side openings, and a correction of its wording that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Background: שמואל explains the שבת storeroom rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in מסכת שבת that forbids clearing out an אוצר, and שמואל explains that this means one may not empty it completely, in case the person comes to level the holes in the floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: There (in מסכת שבת) we learned: 'But not the storeroom.' And שמואל said: What does 'but not the storeroom' mean? It means one may not finish clearing out the whole storeroom, because he might come to level out holes in the floor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next question. It brings a שבת rule, together with שמואל's explanation of it, so that it can compare it to our יום טוב case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in שבת allows moving sacks of produce to make room for guests or for learning, but adds 'not the אוצר.' שמואל explains that you may clear some of it, just not all of it. Once the floor is fully exposed, you might fill in its pits, which is a real מלאכה (building).

keyTerms.meaning: 'There we learned.' This introduces a משנה from a different place in ש״ס.
A storeroom or large pile of stored produce.
He will finish, meaning clear it out completely.
To level out holes or depressions in the floor.
Perhaps, lest. It signals a protective fence (גזירה).

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל does not forbid touching the אוצר at all. Taking some is fine. Only clearing it out completely is forbidden, because that exposes the floor.

phrases.english: There we learned: 'But not the storeroom.'
phrases.notes: משנה in מסכת שבת about clearing sacks for guests and for learning.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
What is the meaning of 'but not the storeroom'?

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא יִגְמוֹר אֶת הָאוֹצָר כּוּלּוֹ,
phrases.english: But he may not finish clearing the entire storeroom,
lest he come to level out holes in the floor.
phrases.notes: Leveling the floor counts as building, which is a full מלאכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new inquiry by importing a שבת rule to compare against the יום טוב משנה about lowering produce through a skylight.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת one may clear sacks from a storeroom but may not empty it entirely, lest one level the floor's holes.

steps.title: The question: does this limit apply to our roof case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is in our case of lowering produce from the roof on יום טוב. May one clear it all, exposing the roof floor?
steps.simpleTranslation: Here (in our case of lowering produce on יום טוב), what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a real question. Does שמואל's rule against emptying the storeroom also apply when lowering fruit from a roof on יום טוב?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lets a person lower produce through a skylight on יום טוב to save it from rain. The open issue is whether he may clear the roof completely, or whether the same worry about leveling the floor limits him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Here, what is the law?' This is a formula for asking a genuine question.

phrases.english: Here, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Refers to lowering produce from the roof on יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the Shabbos rule from step 1 to the יום טוב case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may completely clear the produce off a roof on יום טוב, or whether the 'not the whole אוצר' limit applies.

steps.title: Laying out both sides of the first question
steps.stepSummary: Side 1: the limit exists only because שבת is strict, and יום טוב is lighter. Side 2: on שבת the clearing was for learning and still limited, so on יום טוב, with no מצוה involved, it should be limited all the more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe it is only there, on שבת, that it is forbidden, because שבת is strict. But יום טוב, which is lighter, is fine. Or perhaps: there, where learning in the בית המדרש was at stake, you still said no. Here, where no learning is at stake, all the more so (it is forbidden).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the question is hard. It gives one reason to be lenient on יום טוב and one reason to be even stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lenient side: the שבת fence comes from שבת's greater severity, so it should not carry over to יום טוב. Strict side: the שבת clearing had a מצוה purpose (avoiding בטול בית המדרש) and was still limited. Saving produce on יום טוב is only a money matter, so it deserves even less leniency, a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Strict, severe.
Light, lenient.
It is fine, permitted.
Or perhaps. It introduces the opposite side of a question.
Interruption of learning in the study hall. A מצוה reason for clearing space.
Is it not all the more so? This is the language of a קל וחומר.

steps.confusionAlert: The two sides compare different things. The first compares the strictness of the days (שבת vs. יום טוב). The second compares the purpose of the clearing (a מצוה vs. saving property). That is why each side reaches the opposite result.

phrases.english: It is there, on Shabbat, that it is forbidden,
because it is strict,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יוֹם טוֹב דְּקִיל — שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: but a Festival, which is lighter, it is fine.
Or perhaps:

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם דְּאִיכָּא בִּטּוּל בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ — אָמְרַתְּ לָא,
phrases.english: there, where there is interruption of the study hall, you said no;
phrases.notes: Even with a מצוה reason, the full clearing was not allowed.

phrases.english: here, where there is no interruption of the study hall,
is it not all the more so (forbidden)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two competing lines of reasoning behind the question in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which factor decides the case: the greater severity of שבת (pointing to leniency on יום טוב), or the מצוה purpose present only in the שבת case (pointing to stringency on יום טוב)?
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a recurring pattern: a rule cannot be moved between שבת and יום טוב without asking what its real reason was.

steps.title: Background: רב נחמן limits our משנה to the same roof
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה allows lowering produce through a skylight on יום טוב. רב נחמן limits this to produce on the same roof as the skylight. Carrying it from one roof to another is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here we learned: one may lower produce through a skylight on יום טוב. And רב נחמן said: they taught this only about the same roof, but from roof to roof, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second question, this time in the reverse direction. It quotes a יום טוב rule (with רב נחמן's limit) that it will later compare to שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heter to save produce on יום טוב has a boundary. You may lower it only through an opening in that same roof. Carrying it across to a different roof is too much effort (טרחה) for יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And here we learned.' This introduces our own משנה.
One may lower or drop down (produce).
A skylight, an opening in the roof.
'They taught this only...' It introduces a limitation on a ruling.
From one roof to another roof.

phrases.english: And here we learned:

phrases.aramaic: מַשִּׁילִין פֵּירוֹת דֶּרֶךְ אֲרוּבָּה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One may lower produce through a skylight on a Festival,
And Rav Nachman said:
They taught this only regarding the same roof,
but from roof to roof, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכָא תְּנַן: מַשִּׁילִין פֵּירוֹת דֶּרֶךְ אֲרוּבָּה בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 1: now a יום טוב rule is brought to be compared to שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב one may lower produce only through a skylight in the same roof. One may not carry it from roof to roof.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says one may not carry from roof to roof even when the roofs are level with each other, which supports רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא also teaches this: one may not carry from roof to roof, even when the roofs are at the same height.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רב נחמן, backing up his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds 'even when level.' This means the ban is not only about the extra work of climbing up or down. Moving between roofs at all goes beyond what was permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And a ברייתא also teaches so.' This introduces support from a ברייתא.
One carries or moves (objects).
Equal, level, at the same height.

phrases.english: And it is also taught in a baraita so:
One may not carry from roof to roof
even when their roofs are level.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן's limitation from step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's rule that produce may not be moved from roof to roof on יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'אין מטלטלין מגג לגג אפילו כשגגותיהן שוין.'

steps.title: The reverse question: may sacks move between places on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the 'not roof to roof' limit applies to clearing sacks on שבת. Maybe it applies all the more, since שבת is strict. Or maybe the limit exists only on יום טוב, because people take יום טוב lightly, while שבת needs no such fence.
steps.simpleTranslation: There (on שבת), what is the law? (Is it all the more so forbidden on שבת, which is strict? Or perhaps:) it is here that it is forbidden, because יום טוב is light and people might come to treat it lightly. But שבת, which is strict, and people will not come to treat it lightly, it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the mirror image of its first question and lays out both sides. This time the יום טוב rule is being tested against שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strict side: if this is forbidden even on the lighter יום טוב, then on the stricter שבת it should be forbidden all the more. Lenient side: the יום טוב fence exists because people already take יום טוב lightly, so it needs extra protection. Everyone respects שבת, so no such fence is needed there. Step 7 adds another argument for the strict side, and the series of questions ends with תיקו in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: 'There, what is the law?' This asks about the other case (שבת).
To belittle, to treat lightly.
Which is strict (said of שבת).

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'יום טוב is light' is used in the opposite direction from step 3. There, the lightness of יום טוב suggested leniency. Here, the lightness of יום טוב (people's casual attitude) is exactly why it needs a stricter fence. The same fact can cut both ways.
steps.whatToRemember: Both questions turn on one idea: a fence that exists on one day does not automatically carry over to the other. It depends on why the fence exists, whether because of the day's severity, the purpose of the act, or people's attitude toward the day.

phrases.english: There, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Refers to moving sacks on שבת for guests or learning.

phrases.english: (All the more so on Shabbat, which is strict,
or perhaps:)

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא הוּא דְּאָסוּר — מִשּׁוּם יוֹם טוֹב דְּקִיל,
phrases.english: it is here that it is forbidden, because a Festival is light,
and people would come to belittle it,
but Shabbat, which is strict,
and people will not come to belittle it,
it is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the יום טוב limit from steps 4 and 5 to the שבת sacks case, mirroring the question of steps 2 and 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ban on moving items 'from roof to roof' (or house to house) applies on שבת: all the more so because שבת is stricter, or not at all because the fence was made only for the casually treated יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a fence made because people take יום טוב lightly can actually be stricter on יום טוב than on שבת.

steps.title: Second side: the limit should apply all the more on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The other side of the question: if the roof-to-roof limit applies on יום טוב even though fruit may be lost, then on שבת, where nothing is lost, it should apply all the more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps: here on יום טוב there is a risk of losing the produce, and you still say no. So there, on שבת, where no produce will be lost, shouldn't it be forbidden all the more?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second possible answer to the question from Step 6. It argues that the limit should also apply on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב the produce on the roof could be ruined by rain, and we still forbid carrying it from roof to roof. On שבת, clearing sacks involves no such loss, so there is less reason to be lenient. That means the limit should apply on שבת as well. This is a כל שכן argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. This introduces the other side of a question.
Loss of produce, for example fruit being ruined by rain.
All the more so. This is an argument from the lighter case to the stricter case.
You say (you rule).

phrases.english: Or perhaps:
If here, where there is loss of produce,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the produce on the roof on יום טוב.

phrases.english: you say no (not from roof to roof),
there, where there is no loss of produce,
is it not all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided question begun in Step 6 by giving the second side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the 'not from roof to roof' limit from יום טוב also apply to clearing sacks on שבת?

steps.title: New question: may sacks be lowered by rope or ladder on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: A taught source says that on יום טוב produce may not be lowered with a rope through windows or carried down ladders. The גמרא asks whether this also applies on שבת. First side: maybe on שבת it is allowed, because a place of learning is at stake.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we learned: he may not lower them with a rope through windows, and he may not bring them down by ladders. What is the law there, on שבת? Perhaps here on יום טוב it is forbidden because no learning is being held up. But on שבת, when learning in the בית המדרש is held up, it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second, similar question. It compares the rope-and-ladder limit on יום טוב to clearing sacks on שבת, and gives the first side: on שבת it should be allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב, using ropes or ladders is too much effort just to save fruit, so it is forbidden. On שבת the sacks are being cleared so that people can learn in the בית המדרש. Since a מצוה is involved, perhaps even this extra effort is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Lower them down (with a rope).
Windows.
Ladders.
Holding up (stopping) learning in the study hall.
It is fine, it is permitted.
What is the law there? This is the formula for asking about a parallel case.

phrases.english: Here we learned:
phrases.notes: This refers to produce on the roof on יום טוב.

phrases.english: he may not lower them by rope through windows,
and he may not bring them down by way of ladders.
There (sacks on שבת), what is the law?
Perhaps it is only here, on יום טוב, that it is forbidden,
since there is no holding up of the study hall,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שַׁבָּת, דְּאִיכָּא בִּטּוּל בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ —
phrases.english: but on שבת, where the study hall is being held up,
it is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same יום טוב versus שבת comparison as Steps 6–7, but now about the method of lowering (ropes and ladders).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: On שבת, may sacks be lowered through windows with ropes or down ladders?

steps.title: Second side: on שבת it should be forbidden all the more
steps.stepSummary: The other side: if ropes and ladders are forbidden on יום טוב even when fruit could be lost, then on שבת, with no loss, they should be forbidden all the more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps: here, where produce could be lost, you say no. There, where no produce will be lost, shouldn't it be forbidden all the more?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposite side of the rope-and-ladder question. It uses the same 'loss of produce' argument it used in Step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern about losing fruit is a strong reason to be lenient, and even so, ropes and ladders are not allowed on יום טוב. Clearing sacks on שבת has no money loss at all, so it has an even weaker reason to be lenient. So the method should be forbidden there too.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, meaning the case we already know (יום טוב).
There, meaning the case being asked about (שבת).
Where there is / where there is not.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is word-for-word almost the same as Step 7, but it answers a different question. Step 7 was about moving from roof to roof. This one is about using ropes and ladders.

phrases.english: Or perhaps:
here, where there is loss of produce,
you say no,
there, where there is no loss of produce,
is it not all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the question opened in Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is lowering sacks by rope or ladder on שבת forbidden all the more, because no money is lost?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found, so the question is left open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand (unresolved).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the question without an answer. Both sides were reasonable, and no source decided between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two different ideas pull against each other: holding up learning (a reason to be lenient on שבת) and the lack of money loss (a reason to be strict on שבת). The גמרא cannot decide which one is stronger, so it says תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand. The question remains unresolved.

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא asked three mirror-image questions between שבת and יום טוב. First: may one clear the whole roof on יום טוב? Second: may sacks be moved from roof to roof on שבת? Third: may sacks be lowered by rope or ladder on שבת? In each one the logic pulls both ways. The day's severity, the מצוה of learning, people's attitude to יום טוב, and the loss of produce all point in different directions. No answer is found, and the series ends with תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand (unresolved).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of Steps 8–9 without resolving it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether sacks may be lowered by rope or ladder on שבת is left undecided (תיקו).

steps.title: עולא: covering includes even rows of bricks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, 'one may cover the produce.' עולא says this even includes covering a row of bricks so the rain does not ruin them.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one may cover the produce.' עולא said: even a row of bricks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and gives עולא's explanation. He reads the permission to cover broadly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions only produce. עולא says produce is just an example. Anything that might be ruined by rain, even building bricks, may be covered on יום טוב to prevent the loss.

keyTerms.meaning: One may cover.
עולא, an אמורא.
A row (layer) of bricks.
And even. This marks a widening of the rule.

phrases.english: 'And one may cover the produce.'
עולא said:
And even a row of bricks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic from the משנה, unrelated to the unresolved question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Covering on יום טוב is allowed for anything that could be ruined, even bricks.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: only produce that is fit for use
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק disagrees. One may cover only things like produce that are fit to be used on יום טוב, and not bricks.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: produce that is fit (for use).
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion is given that argues with עולא. רבי יצחק limits the permission to cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יצחק, the word 'produce' in the משנה is exact. It means something fit for use on יום טוב. Bricks are meant for building and are מוקצה, so they may not be covered.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יצחק, an אמורא.
Produce that is fit (for use on the day).
Something set aside, which may not be handled on שבת or יום טוב.

phrases.english: רבי יצחק said:
Produce that is fit (for use).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with עולא's broad reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only items fit for use, like produce, may be covered. Bricks may not.

steps.title: רבי יצחק follows his own rule about handling a vessel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יצחק is consistent. He holds that a כלי may be moved only for the sake of something that may itself be moved on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק follows his own reasoning, for רבי יצחק said: a vessel may be moved only for something that may be moved on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects רבי יצחק's view here to a general rule he says elsewhere. This shows his opinion is not random.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering bricks means handling a cloth (a כלי) for the sake of bricks. Bricks are מוקצה and may not be moved. By רבי יצחק's rule, a כלי may not be handled for something מוקצה, so covering bricks is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning, meaning he is consistent with another statement of his.
A vessel may be moved (handled).
Something that may be moved on שבת (not מוקצה).

steps.whatToRemember: עולא says one may cover anything that could be ruined, even bricks. רבי יצחק says one may cover only usable produce, because a כלי may not be handled for the sake of a מוקצה object.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the argument about covering bricks is really part of a bigger issue: may a permitted כלי be handled to protect מוקצה items?

phrases.english: And רבי יצחק follows his own reasoning.
For רבי יצחק said:
A vessel may not be moved
except for something that may be moved on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grounds רבי יצחק's view from Step 12 in his general rule.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יצחק's limit that only fit produce may be covered.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יצחק's own statement that a כלי may be moved only for something that may be moved on שבת.

steps.title: A proof from the משנה's word 'produce'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says one may cover 'produce,' which suggests that only produce may be covered and bricks may not. That would support רבי יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: 'One may cover produce with coverings.' This implies that produce, yes, may be covered, but a row of bricks, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove רבי יצחק right from the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names 'produce' specifically, and produce may be handled on יום טוב. The גמרא reads this as excluding things like bricks, which are מוקצה. If that reading holds, עולא is contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה)
We may cover
A row of bricks (set out to dry)
Yes / no

phrases.english: We learned: One may cover the produce with coverings.
Produce, yes,
a row of bricks, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to prove רבי יצחק's position, stated in step 12, from the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יצחק's view that only usable items like produce may be covered
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's specific wording 'מכסין את הפירות'

steps.title: 'Produce' was mentioned only to match the earlier clause
steps.stepSummary: The rule may apply to bricks too. The משנה said 'produce' only because its first clause, about lowering produce, used that word.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same law applies even to a row of bricks. But because the first part of the משנה taught 'one may lower produce,' the later part also taught 'one may cover produce.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. The word 'produce' does not exclude bricks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first clause, about lowering items through a skylight, only produce works, because bricks may not be handled at all. The משנה simply kept the same word in the next clause for consistency of style. So the wording proves nothing against עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: The same law applies
Since it taught (style carried over)
First clause / later clause
We may lower (through a skylight)

steps.confusionAlert: The דחיה does not say produce and bricks are the same in every way. Bricks still cannot be lowered. The claim is only that covering them might be allowed.

phrases.english: The same is true even for a row of bricks,
but since it taught in the first clause 'one may lower produce,'

phrases.aramaic: תְּנָא סֵיפָא נָמֵי מְכַסִּין אֶת הַפֵּירוֹת.
phrases.english: it taught in the latter clause too 'one may cover the produce.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes off the proof made in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference drawn from the word 'produce'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wording was chosen to match the earlier clause, not to exclude bricks.

steps.title: A second proof from the wine and oil jugs
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists jugs of wine and oil, which are usable items. This suggests that only usable things may be covered, which would support רבי יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: 'And likewise jugs of wine, and likewise jugs of oil' may be covered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof for רבי יצחק from the משנה's next example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine and oil are fit for use on יום טוב. Since these are the examples given, the משנה seems to allow covering only usable items. That would rule out bricks.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise
Jugs of wine
Jugs of oil

phrases.english: We learned: And likewise jugs of wine
and likewise jugs of oil!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: וְכֵן כַּדֵּי יַיִן וְכֵן כַּדֵּי שֶׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was pushed off, this is a new proof from a different line of the משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's examples of wine and oil jugs

steps.title: The jugs hold untithed wine and oil
steps.stepSummary: The jugs may contain טבל, which may not be used and is מוקצה. If so, the משנה actually allows covering מוקצה items.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Untithed wine and oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second proof. The jugs could hold טבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טבל may not be eaten or used, so it is מוקצה, just like bricks. If the משנה allows covering such jugs, it actually supports עולא, who says even bricks may be covered.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
Untithed produce (טבל), which may not be used

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with here?
With untithed produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 16 by redefining the case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The assumption that the jugs hold permitted, usable liquid
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The jugs could hold טבל, which is מוקצה.

steps.title: Support for reading the jugs as טבל
steps.stepSummary: If the jugs held permitted wine and oil, the example would add nothing, because the משנה already allowed covering produce. So the jugs must be טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too, it is logical. If you think the jugs of wine and oil are permitted, didn't the first clause already teach produce?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the טבל reading by arguing that permitted jugs would be a repetition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה does not usually repeat itself. Permitted wine and oil are no different from permitted produce, which was already mentioned. So the extra example must be teaching something new: that even מוקצה (טבל) may be covered.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is logical
If it enters your mind (if you assume)
Permitted (here: already tithed)

phrases.english: So too it is logical,
for if it enters your mind
that the jugs of wine and jugs of oil are permitted,
didn't it already teach produce in the first clause?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the טבל answer from step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the jugs contain טבל
steps.raayaSupportSource: The principle that a משנה would not repeat an example that adds nothing

steps.title: The jugs teach that even a small loss counts
steps.stepSummary: Permitted jugs are still a needed example. Without them, we might think the חכמים worried only about a large loss, like ruined produce, and not a small loss, like drips into a jug.
steps.simpleTranslation: The jugs of wine and oil were needed. You might have thought that the חכמים were concerned about a large loss but not about a small loss. So the משנה teaches us that even a small loss counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the support from step 18. Permitted jugs do add a new point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rain falling on open produce ruins a lot. A few drops falling into a jug of wine or oil cause only a small loss. The jug example teaches that covering is allowed even to prevent a small loss, so it is not a repetition. Therefore it may be speaking of permitted jugs, and the משנה proves nothing either way.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary for him to teach
A large loss
A small loss
It teaches us (the new point)

steps.whatToRemember: Neither proof from the משנה works. 'Produce' was mentioned only to match the earlier clause. The jugs could be permitted, and they teach that even a small loss counts. So the dispute between עולא and רבי יצחק is not settled by this משנה.

phrases.aramaic: כַּדֵּי יַיִן וְכַדֵּי שֶׁמֶן אִצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Jugs of wine and jugs of oil were necessary for him,
since it could enter your mind to say:
for a large loss, they were concerned,
for a small loss, they were not concerned,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּדֵּי יַיִן וְכַדֵּי שֶׁמֶן אִצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the supporting argument in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that permitted jugs would make the example a repetition
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Permitted jugs add a new point: covering is allowed even to prevent a small loss.

steps.title: Challenge from placing a vessel under a leak
steps.stepSummary: A משנה allows putting a vessel under a leak on שבת. Leak water seems to be מוקצה, so this appears to contradict רבי יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: One may place a vessel under a leak on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק using a משנה. The משנה allows moving a bucket to catch leaking water, even though that water seems unusable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק says you may move a utensil only for the sake of something you are allowed to handle. Dirty leak water looks like מוקצה, yet the משנה lets you move a bucket for it. That seems to break רבי יצחק's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה)
A leak, dripping water from the roof
Something set aside from use on שבת, which may not be handled

steps.confusionAlert: The bucket itself is a permitted utensil. The question is not about the bucket. The question is whether you may move it for the sake of something that is מוקצה, here the leak water.

phrases.english: We learned: One may place a vessel
under a leak on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: The leak water seems unfit to use, so it looks like מוקצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: נוֹתְנִין כְּלִי תַּחַת הַדֶּלֶף בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new series of challenges to רבי יצחק after the discussion of the jugs.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's rule that a utensil may be handled only for something that is not מוקצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows moving a vessel to catch leak water, which seems to be מוקצה.

steps.title: The leak water is usable
steps.stepSummary: The משנה speaks of leak water that is fit to drink, at least for animals, so it is not מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It speaks of a leak whose water is fit to use.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה speaks of clean leak water that can be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the water is drinkable, it is not מוקצה. Moving the bucket to catch it is then moving a utensil for a permitted thing, which matches רבי יצחק.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit, usable

phrases.english: With a leak that is fit for use.
phrases.notes: The water is fit to drink, at least for animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The leak water is unusable and מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of usable water, so it fits רבי יצחק.

steps.title: Challenge from covering bricks
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows spreading a mat over bricks on שבת. רבי יצחק forbade covering bricks.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One may spread a mat over bricks on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge, from a ברייתא that allows covering bricks with a mat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bricks are building material and are normally מוקצה. Earlier, רבי יצחק said you may not cover bricks. This ברייתא says plainly that you may.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, which introduces a source
One may spread a mat
Bricks

phrases.english: Come and hear: One may spread a mat
over bricks on Shabbat!
phrases.notes: This protects the bricks from rain.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: פּוֹרְסִין מַחְצֶלֶת עַל גַּבֵּי לְבֵנִים בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new challenge after step 21 answered the first one.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's ruling that bricks may not be covered
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly allows covering bricks, which seem to be מוקצה.

steps.title: Leftover bricks can be sat on
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא speaks of bricks left over from building. They are no longer set aside for building and are fit to sit on.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are bricks left over from a building, which are fit to sit on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these bricks are leftovers that people use as seats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the building is finished, the extra bricks are no longer meant for building. People sit on them, so they are not מוקצה. Covering them is protecting a usable item.

keyTerms.meaning: Left over from the building
To sit, to recline

phrases.english: That were left over from the building,
which are fit to sit on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bricks are building material and מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: These are leftover bricks used as seats, so they are not מוקצה.

steps.title: Challenge from covering stones
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows spreading a mat over stones on שבת, even though stones are normally מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One may spread a mat over stones on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third challenge, this time about stones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary stones are a classic example of מוקצה. If you may cover them, then you may handle a mat for the sake of מוקצה, against רבי יצחק.

keyTerms.meaning: Stones

phrases.english: Come and hear: One may spread a mat
over stones on Shabbat!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: פּוֹרְסִין מַחְצֶלֶת עַל גַּבֵּי אֲבָנִים בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new challenge after step 23 answered the previous one.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Stones are מוקצה, yet the ברייתא allows covering them.

steps.title: Rounded stones used in the bathroom
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא speaks of smooth, rounded stones. People used them for cleaning in the bathroom, so they are usable on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It speaks of rounded stones, which are fit for use in the bathroom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these are special smooth stones that people used for wiping in the bathroom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These stones had a normal use on שבת, so they are not מוקצה. Covering them protects a permitted item, which fits רבי יצחק.

keyTerms.meaning: Rounded, smooth (stones)
Bathroom, lavatory

phrases.english: With rounded stones,
which are fit for use in the bathroom.
phrases.notes: They were used for personal cleaning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: These are ordinary stones, which are מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: These are rounded stones used in the bathroom, so they are not מוקצה.

steps.title: Challenge from covering a beehive
steps.stepSummary: A source allows spreading a mat over a beehive on שבת, against sun or rain, as long as one does not intend to trap the bees. A beehive seems to be מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One may spread a mat over a beehive on שבת. In the sun, it is to protect against the sun. In the rain, it is to protect against the rain. This is allowed only if he does not intend to trap the bees!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a fourth challenge, about covering a beehive to shield it from sun or rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hive and the bees cannot be used on שבת, so they seem to be מוקצה. Yet the source allows handling a mat to protect them. The only limit it gives concerns trapping, not מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Beehive
To trap (צידה, a forbidden labor on שבת)
Provided that, as long as

phrases.english: Come and hear: One may spread a mat
over a beehive on Shabbat,
in the sun, because of the sun,
and in the rain, because of the rain,
provided that he does not intend to trap!
phrases.notes: Covering the hive could trap the bees inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: פּוֹרְסִין מַחְצֶלֶת עַל גַּבֵּי כַּוֶּרֶת דְּבוֹרִים בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new challenge after step 25 answered the previous one.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A beehive is מוקצה, yet the source allows handling a mat to protect it.

steps.title: The hive contains honey
steps.stepSummary: Here too, the protected item is usable, because the hive has honey in it, and honey may be eaten on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it speaks of a hive that has honey in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last challenge the same way: the hive has honey, which is a usable food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mat is handled for the sake of the honey, which is not מוקצה. So all four sources fit רבי יצחק. Each one protects something that is usable on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: There too
Honey

steps.whatToRemember: Four challenges are raised against רבי יצחק: the leak, the bricks, the stones, and the beehive. Each is answered by showing that the protected item is actually usable on שבת. The honey answer for the beehive will now be tested further, starting in step 28.

phrases.english: There too, it is where there is honey.
phrases.notes: The honey is edible on שבת, so the mat is handled for a permitted thing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 26. This honey answer is itself challenged next by רב עוקבא ממישן (step 28).
steps.terutzMaskana: The hive contains honey, so covering it protects a permitted item.

steps.title: What about winter, when there is no honey?
steps.stepSummary: רב עוקבא מִמֵּישָׁן asks רב אשי: the honey answer works in summer, but the ברייתא also talks about rain, meaning winter, when there is no honey.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוקבא ממישן said to רב אשי: That answer works in the summer, when there is honey in the hive. But in the rainy season, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer, that the hive is usable because it has honey. In winter the hive has no honey, so that answer does not seem to work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spoke of covering the hive against both sun and rain, and rain points to winter. In winter there is no harvestable honey. So the hive should be מוקצה again, and covering it should be a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (but there is still a problem elsewhere)
The summer days
The rainy season, meaning winter
What is there to say?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב עוּקְבָא מִמֵּישָׁן לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Ukva from Meishan said to Rav Ashi:
This works well in the summer,
when there is honey.
But in the rainy season,
what can be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the honey answer of step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the beehive is usable because of its honey
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא mentions rain, which means winter. In winter there is no honey, so the answer fails for part of the case.

steps.title: The two honeycombs left for winter
steps.stepSummary: Even in winter, two honeycombs are left in the hive, and those count as the usable food.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only for those two honeycombs that are left in the hive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: in winter, beekeepers leave two honeycombs in the hive. Those combs are the food that makes the hive usable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The honey answer survives in winter by pointing to the two combs left to feed the bees. So there is still honey in the hive.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (this specific case)
Two honeycombs

phrases.english: It is needed only
for those two honeycombs.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְאוֹתָן שְׁתֵּי חַלּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the winter challenge of step 28
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In winter the hive has no honey, so it is מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even in winter, two honeycombs stay in the hive, so it still has food.

steps.title: Aren't those two honeycombs מוקצה?
steps.stepSummary: The two combs are left on purpose for the bees, so they should be מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But those two honeycombs are מוקצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. Those two combs are set aside for the bees, not for people, so they are off-limits on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something a person sets aside and does not plan to use is מוקצה. The beekeeper leaves these two combs to keep the bees alive through winter. So they should not make the hive usable.

keyTerms.meaning: Set aside, off-limits for use on שבת (plural of מוּקְצֶה)

phrases.english: Those two honeycombs are muktze!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 29
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the two winter honeycombs make the hive usable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The combs are set aside for the bees, so they are מוקצה and cannot count as usable food.

steps.title: He planned to take the combs
steps.stepSummary: The case is where the owner had in mind before the holiday to take those combs for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where he had them in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the case. The owner planned ahead of time to eat those two combs, so they are not set aside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Planning to use an item takes away its מוקצה status. Once the owner had the combs in mind, they are usable. So the hive is not מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrowed case)
He had them in mind, he planned to use them

phrases.english: With what case are we dealing here?
Where he had them in mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מוקצה challenge of step 30
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two combs are set aside for the bees and are מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The owner planned to take them, so they are not מוקצה.

steps.title: Then the ברייתא should have said so
steps.stepSummary: If the rule depends on whether he planned to take the combs, the ברייתא should have made that distinction instead of talking about trapping.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he did not have them in mind, what? It is forbidden? Then instead of teaching 'as long as he does not intend to trap,' let the ברייתא make a distinction within this case itself: 'When is this said? When he had them in mind. But if he did not have them in mind, it is forbidden!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא. If planning ahead is what matters, the ברייתא should have spelled that out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to step 31, a hive whose combs were not planned for would be forbidden to cover. That is a real condition the ברייתא should have mentioned. Instead, the only condition it mentions is not intending to trap the bees.

keyTerms.meaning: Instead of teaching
Let it make a distinction and teach within this case itself
In what case are these words said?
To trap (a forbidden act on שבת)

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא חִשֵּׁב עֲלֵיהֶם מַאי — אָסוּר?
phrases.english: But if he did not have them in mind, what? It is forbidden?
Instead of teaching 'as long as he does not intend to trap,'
let it make a distinction and teach within the case itself:
When is this said?
When he had them in mind,
but if he did not have them in mind, it is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּתָנֵי וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִתְכַּוֵּין לָצוּד לִפְלוֹג וְלִתְנֵי בְּדִידַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the narrowed case of step 31 from the wording of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the ברייתא is about a case where he planned to take the combs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If planning ahead were the key condition, the ברייתא would have stated that condition. It stated a different one, about trapping.

steps.title: Even when he planned it, he still must not intend to trap
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא assumes he had the combs in mind, and adds one more condition: no intent to trap.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: even though he had them in mind, it is allowed only as long as he does not intend to trap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. Planning ahead is assumed in the case, and the ברייתא adds a second condition about trapping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Planning ahead solves the מוקצה problem. There is still a separate problem: covering the hive might trap the bees. So the ברייתא only had to mention the condition that is still open, which is no intent to trap.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying (rereading a text)
Even though

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
even though he had them in mind,
it is allowed only if he does not intend to trap.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחִשֵּׁב עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 32
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The trapping clause replaces the planning condition, so planning ahead must not matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: Planning ahead is assumed, and the trapping clause is an extra condition on top of it.

steps.title: Is the ברייתא half רבי יהודה and half רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: Our explanation treats the ברייתא as following רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה. But its last clause permits an act done without intent, which is the view of רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain the ברייתא? Like רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה? Then look at the last part: 'as long as he does not intend to trap.' Now we have come to רבי שמעון, who says that an act done without intent is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a bigger problem with the whole explanation. It sets up a contradiction that steps 35 and 36 answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds of מוקצה, and he also forbids an act done without intent (דבר שאין מתכוין). רבי שמעון disagrees on both. Our reading uses רבי יהודה for the start of the ברייתא and רבי שמעון for its end, which is a split that does not hold together.

keyTerms.meaning: How did you establish it? (which opinion did you set it as?)
Now say the last clause
We have come to (another opinion)
An act done without intent (a forbidden result he does not intend)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון argue only about מוקצה. They also argue about דבר שאין מתכוין: רבי יהודה forbids it and רבי שמעון permits it. That is why the ברייתא looks split between them.
steps.whyThisMatters: A single ברייתא should follow one consistent opinion. This challenge forces the גמרא to rethink how it explains the beehive case.

phrases.english: How did you explain it?
Like Rabbi Yehuda, who holds of muktze?
Say the last clause:
'as long as he does not intend to trap.'
Now we have come to Rabbi Shimon,
who said: an act done without intent is permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי אוֹקֵימְתָּא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דְּאִית לֵיהּ מוּקְצֶה אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the whole explanation built in steps 29 through 33
steps.kashyaTarget: Explaining the ברייתא with מוקצה, which follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The last clause permits an act done without intent, which only רבי שמעון holds. So the ברייתא would follow two different opinions at once.

steps.title: Even רבי שמעון forbids an unavoidable result
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, because אביי and רבא say רבי שמעון agrees that an unavoidable result (פסיק רישיה) is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really think this follows רבי שמעון? But אביי and רבא both said: רבי שמעון agrees in a case of 'cut off its head, and will it not die?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last question. It says the ברייתא cannot follow רבי שמעון, because even he would forbid covering the hive here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון allows an act done without intent only when the forbidden result might not happen. If the result is certain, like cutting off an animal's head and expecting it not to die, even רבי שמעון forbids it. Covering a beehive that has no other opening always traps the bees, so 'no intent to trap' would not help, even according to רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: And do you really think so? (a phrase that rejects an assumption)
agrees / concedes
'Cut off its head and will it not die?' An act whose forbidden result is certain to happen
Two major אמוראים who often argue, but here they agree

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי שמעון permits every act done without intent. He permits it only when the forbidden result is not certain. When the result is certain (פסיק רישיה), he also forbids it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of פסיק רישיה is a basic principle in הלכות שבת and יום טוב. It limits רבי שמעון's leniency about acts done without intent (דבר שאינו מתכוין).

phrases.english: And do you really think it follows Rabbi Shimon?
But didn't Abaye and Rava both say:
Rabbi Shimon concedes
in a case of 'cut off its head and will it not die?'
phrases.notes: A case where the forbidden result is certain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the premise of step 34 that the last clause of the ברייתא fits רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the ברייתא's permission of an act done without intent follows רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Covering the hive certainly traps the bees, which is a פסיק רישיה, and even רבי שמעון forbids that.

steps.title: The whole ברייתא follows רבי יהודה and the hive has side openings
steps.stepSummary: The whole ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. It is talking about a hive with small side windows, so covering it does not trap the bees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the whole ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. What case are we dealing with here? A hive that has small windows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer. The whole ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, and the case is a hive with extra small openings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the hive has side windows (כַּוֵּי), the bees can still get out after the top is covered. So covering it does not trap the bees at all, and there is no trapping problem even for רבי יהודה, who forbids an unintended act (דבר שאין מתכוין). This keeps the ברייתא fully in line with רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה, which fits steps 30 to 33.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (the גמרא keeps its original approach)
all of it (the whole ברייתא)
What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrower case)
small windows / openings

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the problem is solved by changing the case, not the opinion. Once the hive has side openings, covering it does not trap the bees at all.

phrases.english: Actually, all of it follows Rabbi Yehuda,
and with what case are we dealing here?
Where it (the hive) has small windows.
phrases.notes: So covering the main opening does not trap the bees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem from steps 34 and 35 by placing the whole ברייתא under רבי יהודה and narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's last clause allows an act done without intent, so it seemed to follow רבי שמעון. But that would still be forbidden as a פסיק רישיה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. The hive has side openings, so covering it does not trap the bees at all.

steps.title: Starting to fix the wording of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי יהודה, the ברייתא should not read 'provided he does not intend to trap.' The גמרא begins to correct the wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do not say, according to רבי יהודה, 'provided he does not intend to trap.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a correction of the ברייתא's wording. It says the phrase about intent does not fit רבי יהודה, and the replacement wording comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that an act done without intent is still forbidden if the forbidden result happens. So for him the deciding factor cannot be what the person intends. The words 'no intent to trap' must be changed to describe what actually happens, and that new wording comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: And do not say (the start of a correction of the text)
provided that
he intends
to trap (one of the forbidden מלאכות)

phrases.english: And do not say, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
'provided he does not intend to trap,'
phrases.notes: The corrected wording comes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer in step 36 by fixing the ברייתא's wording so that it fits רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's words about intent seem to follow רבי שמעון's view.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יהודה, the phrase about intent must be replaced with wording about the actual result. The new wording follows on the next amud.
